title: Finite-stratification constructibility for oriented set sheaves
statement: Let $a:X\to S$ and $b:Y\to S$ be morphisms of schemes [def-pc-scheme]. Put $P=X_{\mathrm{Et}}\overleftarrow\times_{S_{\mathrm{Et}}}Y_{\mathrm{Et}}$ using [lem-trf-oriented-product-universal]. A sheaf of sets $F$ on $P$ is constructible if there are finite locally closed scheme stratifications $X=\coprod_\alpha X_\alpha$, $Y=\coprod_\beta Y_\beta$ [def-constructible-stratification], whose strata are constructible subsets [def-weil-constructible-subset], such that the inverse image of $F$ on each oriented rectangle $(X_\alpha)_{\mathrm{Et}}\overleftarrow\times_{S_{\mathrm{Et}}}(Y_\beta)_{\mathrm{Et}}$ is locally constant with finite set values. The rectangle maps are the same induced maps as in [def-trf-oriented-constructible-sheaf], now with sets in place of modules. Explicitly, on each rectangle every site object has a covering sieve such that on each member $V$ the restricted sheaf on the slice at $V$ is isomorphic to the constant sheaf of some finite set [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. No finiteness of the covering sieve is imposed. For $b=1_S$, use the canonical identity-base-change normalization to read this predicate on the vanishing topos $V_a$ of [def-trf-oriented-nearby-cycles].
